```yaml
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featurepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenant:
                type: string
              allowedFlags:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
```

```rego
package gatekeeper.featurepolicy

violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
  annotations := input.review.object.metadata.annotations
  feature := annotations["cnf/feature"]

  not featureR in policy.allowedFlags

}
```

This question tests candidates on multi-cluster configuration distribution, CRD design, real-time propagation mechanisms, and tenant isolation in cloud-native environments.

## Key Concepts

- **Per-tenant feature flags via CRD**: Custom resource definition enabling declarative flag management per tenant

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests understanding of safe, per-tenant traffic experimentation without impacting production. It covers config-driven behavior, sidecar responsibilities, and end‑to‑end validation in a CNF gateway on Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts

- Traffic shadowing (mirroring) to a test shadow target
- Per-tenant configuration via Namespace ConfigMaps
- Fire-and-forget asynchronous forwards
- Deriving shadow path from tenant identity (X-TENANT-ID) and request path
- Observability: simple verification endpoint and metrics

## Code Example

```yaml
# Namespace ConfigMap (per-tenant) - cnf-shadow.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-shadow
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.shadow.enabled: "true"
  cnf.shadow.percent: "10"
  cnf.shadow.target: "shadow-svc.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local"
```

```go
}
```
